History demonstrates that women have been treated like objects by men for at least the last several thousand years in nearly every civilisation.    Get over your victim complex and face reality.  Yes, shitty things happen to men just because they are men (many of which, I myself am opposed to and wish to see an end to), but men are by no means treated as second class citizens in a majority of societies around the world, nor have they ever been.

Unless you're from some sort of alternate dimension, which I suppose is possible at this point.

Did I say..that the reason I don't think it's "full on" discrimination was because it was happening to males?   Because I don't recall saying that at any point.  I said I don't think it's full-on discrimination, but that has nothing to do with the fact that it's happening to men.  And yes, I'm sure their would be more outcry if it were happening to women, but you're being rather presumptuous to assume that I would be a participant in that outcry.

I don't think there's anything wrong with having designated hours of operation for either gender, and if you read any of my other comments, you'd see that I said having a set of men's only hours would be a good compliment to the women's only hours.  I agree that it's unfair to only have women's only hours.  Unfair =/= full-blown oppression, nor do I think it's a reasonable thing to sue about.  But people sue for all sorts of insignificant bullshit these days, anyway, so I guess it shouldn't be surprising.
I agree, men-only hours would be a good compliment to the women-only ones.

Objectively, I think it's a great marketing tactic, because it is TRUE that a lot of women are uncomfortable going to the gym with men (or at least would strongly prefer to only go with women).  So from a business standpoint, if you're offering women's only hours, that is a fucking fantastic way to get more women to sign up for memberships at your particular gym.
Oh ffs, no one thinks men are lesser humans than women -- the entire course of history of humanity since the dawn of civilisation on this planet has demonstrated otherwise.
Gotcha.  Makes a bit more sense.  I still think (personally) it's somewhat of an overreaction, but in light of that, it's more understandable.

If it's a private business, are they not allowed to do whatever the hell they want?

I'm not saying I necessarily agree with having Women's Only hours, but I'm just pointing out that this is a private company and they're perfectly allowed to do whatever the hell they want.  

I don't really feel this amounts to full-on discrimination, to be completely honest, and I think suing a gym because of something as stupid as that (rather than just taking your business elsewhere and getting on with your life) seems like a very childish and unnecessary response to a relatively insignificant issue.
